source.title: Entropy-Guided Token Dropout: Training Autoregressive Language Models with Limited Domain Data
source.authors: Jia-Peng Wang; Yi-Wen Hu; Yanzipeng Gao; Hao-Yu Wang; Shuo Wang; Hong-Yu Lu; Jia-Xin Mao; W. Zhao; J. Li; Xiao Zhang

record.file_problem: The full paper is present, including appendices. Some figure labels and equations are garbled in the extracted text, but the document is not cut off.
record.tranche_reason: The paper cites scaling-law studies but does not test their parameter-, token-, or compute-scaling relationships. It studies validation-loss trajectories during repeated-data training instead.
record.gate_note: The paper reports validation cross-entropy trajectories under multi-epoch training, including by token-entropy group, but does not fit or test scaling laws, extrapolate from smaller runs, compare compute-optimal allocations, or assess architecture effects. Scaling-law mentions are contextual citations. The loss-trajectory results are recorded as findings about the claim's subject, but do not test any listed version.
record.test_reason: The paper proposes entropy-guided token dropout for multi-epoch continual pre-training. It cites Kaplan and Hoffmann only as context. It fits no power laws in parameters, tokens or compute, does no extrapolation, makes no compute-optimal or architecture comparison, and does not test predictability of downstream scores from scale or loss. Its repeated-data results are validation-loss trajectories over training steps and epochs of one fixed-size model, not a scaling-law form, so they do not bear on V5.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is correct. The authors conclude that multi-epoch degradation possibly stems from overfitting on low-entropy tokens while high-entropy generalization degrades. EntroDrop delays overfitting across 0.6B–8B models. They draw no conclusion about scaling-law versions, only a general remark that effective scaling can come from better data use.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies entropy-guided token dropout for repeated-data continual pre-training, not a scaling-law fitting or extrapolation method.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that dropout schedule and maximum masking ratio affect training dynamics and downstream accuracy; masking too strongly from the outset slows early learning.

fits_no_version.finding: Under heavy repetition of a 0.1B-token math set, accuracy peaks around 50 epochs and then declines. High-entropy token validation loss rebounds while low-entropy loss stays near zero. Token dropout delays the validation-loss minimum from about epoch 25 to 50–125 (Table 4).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Multi-epoch repetition of scarce data causes validation loss to rebound, concentrated on high-entropy tokens; input-level dropout delays the rebound.

record.problems: The loss-trajectory evidence relevant to the subject is described qualitatively and shown in figures without numeric values or uncertainty estimates. The paper does not test scaling-law fits or extrapolations.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant loss-trajectory findings omitted. Downstream benchmark comparisons and regularization ablations were excluded because they do not test a listed scaling-law version.

untested.parts: Whether power-law form holds under repeated data or other regimes; no scale sweep or fit.
Benchmarks are reported for 0.6B, 1.7B and 8B, but not analysed as scale-predictable. Token budgets and base models differ.

record.verdict_notes: The record's relation (cites_only) and tranche (T6) are confirmed. The Table 4 min validation loss and best epoch values are method-ablation results, so omitting them is fine.
